links.outcome: Reader AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and interpretation time with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: AUC rose 68.9% to 90.9% (p<0.001); sensitivity 88.5% vs 54.2%; specificity 87.9% vs 80.7%; inter-reader agreement 72% vs 26%; time 23 vs 40 s per image.
links.quote: With AI assistance, AUC presented a mean improvement of 21.9 percentage points (68.9% to 90.9%, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Clinician performance with AI assistance versus unassisted reading in a multi-reader study
links.effect: Sensitivity improved 88.5% vs 54.2% (p<0.01) and specificity 87.9% vs 80.7% (p<0.01) with AI assistance.
links.quote: With AI, sensitivity was overall improved (88.5% vs. 54.2%, p < 0.01), as was specificity (87.9% vs. 80.7%, p < 0.01), inter-reader agreement (72% vs 26%) and interpretation time (23 vs 40 s per image).

screen.practice: AI assistance versus unassisted clinician reading (human-AI reader support)
screen.reason: This is a multireader multicase study evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of clinicians reading fetal ultrasound images with versus without an AI decision-support tool. It evaluates baseline human-AI interaction/model efficacy rather than testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
